title: A reported first platform Tribunal hearing establishes institutional use without an observed worker remedy
source_unit: One reported GrabCar proceeding before Malaysia's Gig Workers Tribunal; case-level procedural record, not a worker sample
geography: Kuching, Sarawak, Malaysia; comparative case used in the US-centered atlas

first_hearing_reported.unit: GrabCar proceeding reported as reaching a first hearing

respondent_employee_representation.unit: GrabCar reported as represented by an employee

observations.method: Bounded case-level extraction from two independent public reports attributing the hearing facts to Malaysia's Ministry of Human Resources/Gig Workers Tribunal.
observations.uncertainty: The primary case number, filed claim, relief sought, hearing notice, transcript, and Tribunal reasoning are not public in the checked packet.
observations.subgroup: One e-hailing gig worker and GrabCar Sdn Bhd in a reported Kuching proceeding.
observations.counterinterpretation: A reported hearing establishes institutional use, not effective review, a meritorious claim, correction, payment, or restored platform access.

observations.method: Cross-source comparison of the first-hearing reports and the local case record; procedural continuation is kept separate from a final adjudication.
observations.uncertainty: The next hearing date, pleadings, evidence, settlement, award, enforcement, and worker-level consequence are not identified in the available public reports.
observations.subgroup: Same reported GrabCar Tribunal proceeding after first hearing.
observations.counterinterpretation: A matter moving to evidence can remain unresolved, inaccessible, or produce no correction or payment; hearing progress is not recovery.

observations.subgroup: Same reported GrabCar proceeding; official-public-record visibility boundary.
observations.counterinterpretation: The case may have advanced outside the public search surface; the current evidence supports institutional use but not claimant outcome.

boundary: This is one reported comparative Malaysian proceeding, not a worker prevalence estimate, compliance audit, or finding that the platform violated Act 872. It distinguishes institutional establishment, reported hearing use, evidence-stage continuation, primary case identification, award, payment, access correction, durability, trust, and exit.
